symptom: `diff-local` counted a changed nanoflow or layout as modified and printed no hunk — after mendixlabs/mxcli#1393 fixed the same for pages
cause: Both renderers in cmd_diff_local.go emitted a fixed placeholder body (`-- (nanoflow body)`, `-- (layout structure)`). Nanoflows never even reached theirs: the dispatch tested `strings.Contains(unitType, "Microflow")` first, and `Microflows$Nanoflow` contains it, so the microflow parser got the document, returned nil, and both sides became the same `parse failed` stub
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_diff_local.go` (dispatch order, nanoflowBsonToMDL, layoutBsonToMDL), `mdl/backend/microflow.go` + `modelsdk/microflow_parse_raw.go` (ParseNanoflowFromRaw; regenerate unimplemented_gen.go / mcp unsupported_gen.go), `cmd_microflows_show.go` (nanoflowAsMicroflow), `cmd_pages_describe.go` (layoutWidgetsFromRawData)
insight: **A `strings.Contains` dispatch over storage type names is ordered by containment, not by taste**: `Microflows$Nanoflow` ⊃ "Microflow", `Forms$PageTemplate` ⊃ "Page", `Security$ModuleSecurity` ⊃ "Module". Before adding a case, list which other $Types contain its needle. A mock parser that accepts any $Type hides this — make mocks refuse foreign types the way the real backend does, which is what made the unit test catch the dispatch. Reuse the DESCRIBE renderers via a raw-data variant of their `get…FromRaw(ctx, id)` extractors rather than writing a second renderer (#997's lesson)
